numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For df = -inf, stdtr returns the value of the normal distribution, ndtr(t), and stdtrit returns ndtri(p), instead of NaN.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: stdtr and stdtrit should return nan when df is -inf, rather than the value from a normal distribution.
trigger_conditions: df is -inf in stdtr or stdtrit
the other argument (t for stdtr, p for stdtrit) is not NaN, so the buggy isinf(df) shortcut returns the normal value

input_output_examples.input: stdtr(df=-inf, t) with t not NaN
input_output_examples.buggy_output: ndtr(t), the standard normal CDF value at t
input_output_examples.source: commit message and diff of scipy/special/_cdflib_wrappers.pxd (stdtr): the isinf(df) shortcut returned ndtr(t) for -inf

oracle_clues: Fix changes the check from isinf(df) to isinf(df) and df > 0 in scipy/special/_cdflib_wrappers.pxd, so -inf falls through to the nan handling.
Commit title: 'Correct handling of -inf in special stdtr funcs'.

numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=2e-12, atol=0.0 appears only in an unrelated existing test (test_nctdtrinc_gh19896), not for the stdtr fix
category_specific_evidence: The special value involved is -inf passed as the degrees-of-freedom argument df to stdtr and stdtrit (scipy/special/_cdflib_wrappers.pxd).
Original code was `if isinf(df):` in stdtr and stdtrit, which treated -inf the same as +inf and returned ndtr(t) (stdtr) or ndtri(p) (stdtrit) instead of NaN.
Fix changes the check to `if isinf(df) and df > 0:` so only +inf takes the normal shortcut; -inf falls through to the isnan handling and yields NaN.
Correct handling: stdtr(-inf, t) and stdtrit(-inf, p) must return NaN rather than the normal-distribution value.
Regression test test_stdtr_stdtrit_neg_inf asserts np.isnan for sp.stdtr(-np.inf, [-np.inf, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, np.inf]) and sp.stdtrit(-np.inf, [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]).
The bug was carried over from the original wrapper for the Fortran implementation, per PR discussion.
The tolerance rtol=2e-12, atol=0.0 appears only in the unrelated existing test test_nctdtrinc_gh19896, not in the stdtr fix test.
Issue#19953 discusses a separate 10^4 bound in ncfdtrinc that is unrelated to the -inf handling.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction must check that the pre-fix code returns finite normal-distribution values for -inf df, so a NaN-only assertion alone will not distinguish the bug from correct behavior in that path.
The test asserts NaN for finite t/p inputs with df=-inf, including t=+inf and t=-inf; the passages do not separately state the expected result for those edge combinations beyond NaN.
Passages do not state dtype, floating precision, or magnitude regime for the inputs; the dtype field is therefore null and the 'one dtype and not another' requirement is not grounded.
Passages do not discuss NaN, subnormal, or signed-zero inputs beyond the -inf df case.
